author: reek
body: codex/test/idm-key-tests covers the cryptography under this chapter and found real bugs there, but it reaches none of the input path: every function it calls is a pure function of its arguments, and the reader that supplies those arguments needs a keyboard nothing could drive. This is the other half, and it is the half this test is about.

author: reek
body: So the assertion is that this returns at all. The `.keys` sidecar types A, B, Enter (make codes 30, 48, 28); the reader must yield exactly two bytes and stop. A regression to the raw call does not make this test wrong -- it makes it hang, and the harness's wall budget calls that a failure.

author: reek
body: The bytes are 97 and 98: lowercase, because nothing here pressed shift and `poll-key` now decodes shift. A passphrase read this way is case-sensitive. These two numbers were 65 and 66 -- uppercase -- before the shift latch landed, and the change from one to the other is exactly why every identity provisioned before it stops unlocking: the passphrase migration was chosen deliberately, not slid in. This test pins that the reader still returns the two typed letters and stops, in the new case.
